title: Hidden in Plane Sight: Finding Lost Airplanes Before Time Runs Out

notes: All 61 UTF-8 page-text files were read sequentially, with Summary and Introduction studied before the remaining substantive chapters.
Eighteen one-at-a-time JPEG proxies, each no larger than 450,000 bytes, covered pages 1-61 in three fresh contexts; no original full-page PNG entered model context.

All 23 numbered equations were reconciled by page, all 37 numbered figures and five substantive unnumbered tables have source-ordered dispositions, and no clipping, overlap, blank page, black box, missing glyph, or formula-rendering defect was found.

section_map.summary: Input: An aircraft missing over remote water, rescue urgency, uncertain crash location, and finite search resources. Analytical job: Preview a bounded Gaussian location field, random and systematic route simulations, Bayesian updating, completion proportions, and transfer to different targets/resources. Output: A conditional promise that posterior-guided searching can find most modeled crashes quickly enough to matter for rescue. Handoff: The contents and introduction unpack the research, assumptions, candidate routes, realism upgrade, evidence, and recommendation.

Input: The summary's location-to-route-to-recommendation promise. Analytical job: Order research, variable/scenario foundation, assumptions, two model regimes, stability tests, comparative results, recommendation, public communication, and provenance. Output: A complete source-heading map in which ideal and uncertainty-aware solutions remain visibly distinct. Handoff: Introduction supplies the ranked human criteria that give this architecture its decision purpose.

Input: Modern aircraft can still disappear over open ocean while families and possible survivors wait. Analytical job: Prioritize discovery, then rescue time; include aircraft/sensor variation; route case research, variables, geometry, simulation, imperfect detection, stability, and analysis. Output: A two-level objective and an auditable research-to-decision work plan. Handoff: Historical and technical research select the incident class, lost-plane trigger, probability objective, and sensor regime.

Input: A broad class of ocean disappearances with heterogeneous aircraft, causes, communication systems, and search technologies. Analytical job: Use Earhart/MH370 as context; screen 89 cases; choose Atlantic passenger aircraft and three representatives; exclude ATC/hijacking cases; set a 30-minute uncertainty interval; define containment times detection; choose P-8 radar. Output: A modelable Atlantic mid-flight crash case with a representative target set, lost-contact window, probability objective, and initial ideal sensor. Handoff: Variables and scenario calculations translate those research choices into geometry and simulation parameters.

Input: The selected incident class, representative aircraft, 30-minute alert rule, search-theory probabilities, and P-8 radar. Analytical job: Define lost/search states; derive glide range and 30-minute path length; create a swept-capsule rectangle; select Boeing 777 values; simplify containment to uniform x and normal y; choose P-8 speed and sight. Output: A 520-by-200-mile coordinate search field, probability representation, selected target/search aircraft, and symbol interface. Handoff: General assumptions freeze the regime in which these inputs may be used.

Input: The rectangle, containment model, representative aircraft, sensor, and search-time objective. Analytical job: Fix flat geometry, no wind/current, on-route instantaneous failure, bounded glide, stationary debris, ideal mobilization/endurance/weather/cost, and uniform radar sight. Output: A controlled ideal regime whose known gaps can later motivate discovery uncertainty and final limitations. Handoff: The normal-distribution model instantiates the common crash generator, completion rule, and statistical protocol.

section_map.section: 5 Models / 5.1 Normal Distribution / Completed Simulation / Statistical Analysis
section_map.summary: Input: A rectangular normal-containment field, ideal radar, search-plane motion variables, and candidate route requirement. Analytical job: Sample crashes from the normal field; stop when distance is below sight range; summarize time by mean, median, spread, standard error, and 95-percent confidence interval. Output: A reusable simulation harness and comparison metric for ideal-discovery paths. Handoff: Random paths establish failure, confinement, and weighting baselines within that harness.

Input: The shared crash field, ideal completion rule, P-8 speed/sight, and a need for a comparison baseline. Analytical job: Update a random unit vector; redirect excursions orthogonally; add endpoint weighting; run 100 trials where feasible; compare skewed time distributions and overlapping intervals. Output: An unviable unbounded route and two slow, redundant bounded baselines with no proven difference between them. Handoff: Systematic routes directly repair overlap and probability-ordering failures.

section_map.section: Solution 5.1.4 / Solution 5.1.5 / Solution 5.1.6 / Normal Distribution Overall Conclusion
section_map.summary: Input: Random-route redundancy, a normal containment field, 10-mile sight, and the common ideal-detection harness. Analytical job: Test edge-to-edge descending stripes, center-out alternating stripes, and sight-scaled sinusoidal passes; measure 100-trial time distributions and interval overlap. Output: Systematic routes dominate random baselines; center-out spiral stripes give the lowest one-plane ideal-model times. Handoff: Discovery uncertainty tests whether the ideal-model winner remains preferable when passes can miss debris.

section_map.section: 5.2 Normal Distribution with Discovery Uncertainty / Solution 5.2.1 / Solution 5.2.2
section_map.summary: Input: The same containment field and route family, now with separate radar and operator failure probabilities. Analytical job: Set detection from radar and operator terms; update searched/unsearched containment after nondetection; choose posterior maxima for each pass; cap at 24 hours; compare 500 adaptive and fixed-route trials. Output: Bayesian search has a higher conditional mean but finds 95 percent by 24 hours versus 80 percent for fixed spiral stripes, with equal medians. Handoff: Stability scenarios alter target detectability and search resources before aggregate results choose a recommendation.

Input: The Bayesian winner, the ideal spiral/stripe geometry, Boeing target properties, and one P-8 search plane. Analytical job: Shrink the area and detection rate for a Cessna; then add a second plane with opposite, nonoverlapping striped motion; compare distributions and intervals. Output: Target size materially changes Bayesian search time, while a second idealized plane lowers stripe-search mean to about 2.4 hours. Handoff: Results synthesize all route and stability evidence by model regime.

Input: Seven ideal-route trials, three uncertain-discovery trials, confidence intervals, skew diagnostics, medians, and 24-hour failure counts. Analytical job: Establish systematic-versus-random differences; identify two-plane and one-plane ideal winners; compare uncertain routes by median and completion proportion; compare target sizes. Output: Spiral stripes win the one-plane ideal model, but the Bayesian route wins the realistic decision because its equal median accompanies much higher completion. Handoff: Recommendation ties that statistical tradeoff back to the rescue-time criterion.

Input: Rescue-before-hypothermia criterion, ideal-route times, uncertain-route medians, and 24-hour completion proportions. Analytical job: Reject idealized solutions despite sub-eight-hour means; compare equal 4.05-hour medians; prefer 95-percent Bayesian completion over 80-percent spiral completion. Output: Recommend the normal distribution with discovery uncertainty paired with a Bayesian-adjusted flight path. Handoff: Strengths and weaknesses delimit what that recommendation actually supports.

Input: The chosen Bayesian mechanism, Boeing/Cessna completion evidence, confidence interval, and all earlier idealizations. Analytical job: Attribute flexibility to adjustable detection/area/sight inputs; report completion and rescue-window evidence; identify exponential computation, overlap, distribution uncertainty, omitted drift/weather/debris stages, mobilization, fuel, and cost. Output: A bounded recommendation with explicit computational, geometric, physical, temporal, and resource failure modes. Handoff: The press document translates the intended procedure for a public audience while some technical caveats become less explicit.

Input: Public concern after MH370 and the paper's posterior-guided search loop. Analytical job: Predict from last signal/path; bound and deploy; fly parallel paths; update location from search data; adjust for equipment imperfections; continue and refine. Output: A stakeholder-facing commitment to rapid, thorough, adaptive searching. Handoff: References document the external evidence and software behind the technical paper.

Input: Historical cases, aircraft specifications, communication rules, search theory, radar tests, Bayesian formulas, visual-search evidence, survival data, images, and software. Analytical job: Map citations to incidents, specifications, detection assumptions, probability updating, and rescue timing; identify Mathematica/Excel and image dependencies. Output: A provenance boundary lacking frozen code, simulation datasets, random seeds, posterior grids, and executable configurations. Handoff: This closes the source; no later section repairs the missing reproducibility artifacts.

assumptions.summary: The lost aircraft follows a straight route, fails within a fixed half-hour window, and glides according to representative speed, altitude, and glide ratio.
The search domain is open ocean and is represented as a rectangle around the candidate flight segment.
Crash x is uniform and cross-track y follows the selected normal containment model.
The P-8 flies at constant speed and ideal trials detect every target inside a fixed 10-mile radius.
Weather, fatigue, refueling, turn time, coordination conflicts, currents, debris drift, and sea-state effects are excluded from the path simulations.
Uncertain trials use radar success 0.8, round operator recognition from 0.97 to one, and cap runs at 24 hours.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Historical missing-aircraft and MH370 context motivates an Atlantic open-ocean case; these sources are contextual rather than a statistical training population.
Two notation tables define lost-plane and search-state variables before their equations, although later symbols drift.
B777, G450, and C172 specifications are compared; the B777 baseline fixes 640 mph, 35,000 ft, 15:1 glide, r=100 mi, and L=320 mi.
P-3 and P-8 specifications are compared; the P-8 baseline fixes 400 mph and a 10-mile sensor radius.
The crash sampler generates 5,000 points for prior inspection and separate route experiments use 100 trials under ideal detection.
Discovery-uncertainty experiments use 500 trials and retain successful times separately from completion proportions.

models.summary: Define discovery success as the product of containment and detection so location priors and sensor performance remain separate.
Construct a rectangular candidate region from aircraft glide reach and the distance traveled during the uncertain failure interval.
Sample crash locations uniformly along the flight direction and normally across it, stop a path at detection, and summarize discovery time with histograms and approximate confidence intervals.
Generate a baseline search path from normalized random vectors without enforcing the search boundary.
Keep random search steps inside the rectangular domain by redirecting out-of-bounds coordinates toward its center axes.
Bias random motion toward the farther endpoint to spend more time near the normal distribution's center while retaining stochastic exploration.
Sweep parallel horizontal tracks from the high-probability center downward with vertical spacing equal to one radar diameter.
Sweep horizontal tracks in an alternating center-out order to cover the highest-probability bands before the tails.
Replace straight horizontal stripes with a sinusoidal tangent-stepping path while preserving alternating center-out coverage.
Update searched-cell containment after imperfect detection, choose the next high-probability stripe, and compare adaptive Bayesian and fixed spiral routes under a 24-hour cap.
Compare target classes, one versus two search planes, route distributions, completion proportions, and rescue timing to recommend Bayesian adaptive search with explicit scope limits.

dependency_graph.handoff: Containment and detection factors define the discovery criterion used by the simulation harness.
Glide range r and uncertain distance L define the 520-by-200-mile B777 simulation domain and crash prior support.
The common crash sampler and detection-time statistics evaluate the unbounded random route.
The same crash samples, rectangle, and stopping rule evaluate bounded random search.
Boundary control is retained while endpoint-directed bias modifies the bounded random route.
The common ideal-detection harness evaluates descending stripes.
Straight stripe coverage is reordered center-out using alternating vertical transitions.
The center-out ordering is retained while each stripe becomes sinusoidal.
The Gaussian containment prior and detection harness become a discrete posterior grid with imperfect discovery.
The ideal spiral route supplies the fixed-path comparator under discovery uncertainty.
Bayesian/spiral success proportions and conditional time distributions enter the final comparison.
Descending-stripe results enter the route comparison and two-plane extension.
Ideal spiral results establish the best one-plane ideal-detection baseline.
Sinusoidal results provide the final systematic-route alternative.
Aircraft geometry is changed for the C172 transfer check.

verification.limitation: Turn dynamics and implementation ambiguities remain shared or route-specific.

verification.summary: Bayesian and fixed spiral routes report 500-trial completion counts and conditional time distributions.

verification.limitation: Detection is linearly scaled by aircraft area without calibration.

verification.summary: A two-plane striped route tests one resource extension.
verification.strength: Aircraft count reaches the decision layer.
verification.limitation: No coordination, separation, staging, or refueling model is tested.

results_trace.summary: Bounded random: 100 trials, median 24.425 h, mean 42.7105 h, interval [33.2348,52.1862].
Weighted bounded random: median 16.6 h, mean 37.5575 h, interval [26.4795,48.6755]; overlap is descriptive, not a formal test.
Descending stripes: median 7.031 h and mean 7.10273 h.
Ideal spiral stripes: median 3.113 h and mean 3.62286 h, the best one-plane ideal-detection result.
Sinusoidal route: median 4.489 h and mean 6.44989 h.
Bayesian B777: 475/500 found, median 4.05 h and success-conditional mean 6.21463 h.
Uncertain spiral B777: 399/500 found, median 4.05 h and success-conditional mean 4.76078 h.
Bayesian C172: 411/500 found, median 6.435 h and success-conditional mean 8.38549 h.
Two-plane stripes: 100 trials, median 2.1435 h and mean 2.39551 h.
The paper recommends normal containment with discovery uncertainty and a Bayesian-adjusted route, prioritizing higher completion despite conditional-time tradeoffs.

contributions.summary: Containment and detection are separated conceptually before route design.
Aircraft state is converted into an explicit bounded search geometry.
One crash sampler and statistical harness support a route-learning ladder from weak random baselines to center-first systematic paths.
Alternating spiral stripes align route order with the cross-track prior rather than only enforcing geometric coverage.
Missed detections update searched and unsearched cell probabilities, linking sensing uncertainty to adaptive route choice.
Target-size and aircraft-count scenarios probe two practical transfer axes.
A separate press document translates the modeled procedure into stakeholder-facing operations.

writing_logic.summary: abstract: Make the whole paper legible as an escalation from location prediction and ideal route screening to imperfect discovery and a final decision. The contents and introduction unpack the research, assumptions, candidate routes, realism upgrade, evidence, and recommendation.

title: Expose the unusually long evidence route before the reader enters historical research or simulation detail. Introduction supplies the ranked human criteria that give this architecture its decision purpose.

introduction: Rank success criteria and show that the proposed recommendation will be earned through a declared sequence rather than asserted immediately. Historical and technical research select the incident class, lost-plane trigger, probability objective, and sensor regime.

problem-analysis: Narrow the modeling case through explicit historical, geographic, causal, regulatory, and sensing choices. Variables and scenario calculations translate those research choices into geometry and simulation parameters.
notation: Bind every later equation and path rule to named physical or operational quantities before simulation begins. General assumptions freeze the regime in which these inputs may be used.

assumptions: Make the first experiment's idealizations inspectable and organize them by environment, crash, and search operation. The normal-distribution model instantiates the common crash generator, completion rule, and statistical protocol.

model-establishment: Give every route a shared test bed and reporting template so comparisons do not change the target or stopping rule. Random paths establish failure, confinement, and weighting baselines within that harness.
algorithm: Reveal why unconstrained randomness, boundary confinement, and weak containment weighting remain inadequate. Systematic routes directly repair overlap and probability-ordering failures.

model-improvement: Make each new geometry a traceable repair and compare it on the same outcome distribution. Discovery uncertainty tests whether the ideal-model winner remains preferable when passes can miss debris.

robustness-verification: Increase realism without losing comparability by changing the observation model and explicitly showing its effect on the next action. Stability scenarios alter target detectability and search resources before aggregate results choose a recommendation.

sensitivity-robustness: Test flexibility by changing recognizable scenario dimensions instead of repeating the baseline with cosmetic inputs. Results synthesize all route and stability evidence by model regime.

results: Prevent a single fast conditional mean from dominating by separating regimes and matching statistics to skew/censoring. Recommendation ties that statistical tradeoff back to the rescue-time criterion.
conclusion: Choose the most defensible route by the ranked objective rather than merely the smallest reported mean. Strengths and weaknesses delimit what that recommendation actually supports.

strengths-limitations: Preserve the recommendation's adaptive value while preventing its modeled rescue performance from being mistaken for field validation. The press document translates the intended procedure for a public audience while some technical caveats become less explicit.
memo: Translate technical work into accountable immediate actions without introducing a new mathematical claim. References document the external evidence and software behind the technical paper.

references: Expose the external basis of major choices while revealing what cannot be reconstructed from the paper alone. This closes the source; no later section repairs the missing reproducibility artifacts.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The Summary routes urgency through geometry, simulation, uncertainty, transfer, and recommendation with explicit numbers; award status does not establish which move caused judging success.
Shared-scale comparison plots make route tradeoffs scannable, while their statistical interpretation remains bounded.
The press document closes the technical-to-stakeholder loop without proving operational deployment readiness.

weaknesses.summary: Equation 2 multiplies a dimensionless glide ratio by altitude in feet but reports r in miles without an explicit feet-to-miles conversion. Preserve the source expression and require a typed conversion before numeric reuse.

Equation 4 visibly compares the vector difference S_i-(x_crash,y_crash) with scalar d without a norm, and the crash-coordinate notation conflicts with the earlier (x_c,y_c) table. A runnable detector needs a scalar distance and one coordinate contract.

Equations 6, 11, 13, and 16 advance the search plane with v even though v was defined for the lost aircraft and v_s for the search plane. The implementation must resolve the symbol rather than silently assuming 400 mph.

Equations 7, 8, and 12 use the set-union symbol between Boolean boundary conditions. Corner precedence, simultaneous x/y violations, and equality behavior are also omitted, so the printed rule is not an executable boundary contract.

The weighted random path fixes a factor of 15 without calibration or sensitivity analysis. Its confidence-interval overlap with bounded random is treated as no significant difference, although interval overlap is not the reported hypothesis test.

Equations 14 and 17 define C(u) as a dimensionless alternating integer while the route uses it as a physical stripe displacement. The visually printed formulas appear to omit a sight-range scale such as d.

Equation 15 does not make clear whether C(j) is an absolute vertical coordinate or an incremental displacement, nor whether j and epsilon update before or after the move. Preserve this ambiguity in any transcription.

Equation 18 adds scalar C(j)r to vector S_i, reuses r from lost-aircraft glide range, and flips epsilon although its downstream role is unclear. The printed transition is dimensionally and algorithmically incomplete.

The source rounds a cited 97-percent operator recognition probability to one, raising P(D_u) from about 0.776 to 0.8. Its minimum-90-second view claim assumes a full 20-mile diameter crossing and does not cover a marginal target encounter.

The Bayesian B777 interval is arithmetically inconsistent: 6.21463 plus or minus 2(0.246568) gives a lower bound about 5.72149, not 5.57215. The page also describes samples of size 100 although this run used 500 trials and 475 successes.

Uncertain-model means and intervals omit trials not found by 24 hours. Comparing Bayesian 95-percent completion with spiral 80-percent completion through success-conditional intervals does not compare overall time-to-discovery distributions; censoring or restricted-time analysis is required.

The C172 discovery probability is produced by linearly scaling rectangular aircraft size from the B777 to 2 percent. No evidence shows radar/debris detectability is proportional to that geometric area, and the reported SD/SE imply a sample count inconsistent with 411 successes.

The abstract attributes an average time of about 4.7 hours to the Bayesian method, while the body reports Bayesian mean 6.21463 hours; 4.76078 hours belongs to the uncertain spiral route. The recommendation must use route-labeled result records.

The paper dates MH370's departure as March 4, 2014 rather than March 8, and page 6 states that Amelia Earhart fragments were finally found although its cited context remains unresolved. These contextual facts require source verification before reuse.

Page 56 visibly ends the sentence 'Furthermore, the Bayesian Solution' before the recommendation, and page 61 labels image references as 8.2 after Section 10. These are genuine source organization/provenance defects rather than extraction clipping.

Formulate multi-aircraft posterior coverage with staging, separation, turns, fuel, communication, overlap, and dynamic reassignment.
